issues.description: The problem text and UML refer to a method named printFarmSong() to play the song, but the template and the solution define and expect a method named singFarmSong(). This name/ signature mismatch between the specification and the provided code can confuse students about which method to implement and which name the tests or Main will call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the method in the template and solution to printFarmSong(), and update any callers (and the UML/spec) accordingly, or change the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong(). Ensure the template method stub and the expected method name in the specification/tests match exactly.

issues.description: The template's private helper method singFarmSongVerse is declared without a parameter (the parameter is commented out), but the UML in the problem statement and the solution implementation expect singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). If students implement singFarmSong() and try to call singFarmSongVerse(animal) following the UML/spec, the template signature will cause a compilation error.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the parameter on the template helper method so its signature matches the UML and solution: change the method declaration to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) and update the stub body accordingly. Also, ensure any calls from singFarmSong() in the template use that parameter (e.g., singFarmSongVerse(animal)).

issues.description: The problem specification refers to a Farm method named printFarmSong(), but both the template and the solution implement and reference a method named singFarmSong(). This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual operation (playing/singing the farm song) can confuse students: they may look for printFarmSong() in the starter code and tests, fail to find it, or implement the wrong method name, breaking mappings between requirements and code.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across artifacts. Either update the problem statement to reference singFarmSong() as the method to implement (recommended to match the template/solution), or rename the method in the template and solution to printFarmSong(). Ensure all references in the Main, UML, and task descriptions use the same identifier.
